cells.tense: Right now you are reading how much to add and how much to hold back.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Pass on something you were taught, the way you got it, with one change of your own. Then leave it with whoever takes it up, and don't stand over how they hold it.
cells.core:
You are good at this part: sensing what a moment needs, adding less here, more there, keeping the whole thing moving without freezing it. That is not a middle ground you retreat to. It is a live adjustment, and it works because you are actually present to what is happening. What you pass on carries some of you in it, and it still fits the people who receive it.

Give one of those teachings away this month and change one thing as you hand it over — your own wording, or what you add at the end. You will want to hover once it leaves your hands, to make sure it is kept the right way. Let it land as theirs. The living part was not the exact shape of it, and you will see that once you stop standing over it.
cells.sheetLine: What you hand on stays alive because you change one thing.

cells.tense: You will have the next step already arranged before the feeling has even asked.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one step today toward what you actually want, before you have settled how it sits with the others close to you. Small is fine. Let the unease be there without fixing it first.
cells.core:
The adjusting is not wrong — it is just running ahead of you. A gathering gets its shape settled before it starts, a difference gets rounded off before anyone has to feel it, and by the time the moment arrives there is nothing left to read. The flow is smooth and it is not yours. Something in you is bracing for a future that has not asked anything of you yet.

Under all of that there is something you genuinely want, and it has a direction. Move one step toward it today — not the whole plan, just the step the feeling is already leaning into. The next piece of resistance will show up and you can keep going through it. The point is not to be less careful. It is to let what you want pick the direction, so the tuning has something real to work with.

cells.tense: You have been standing in many places at once and none of them have held.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Sit with someone in something hard and don't fix it. A few minutes is enough. Let it be unfinished when you both get up.
cells.core:
Down here nothing holds. Each gathering, each conversation, pulls you its own way, and you come out of them further from a center than when you went in. The adjusting itself may still be happening — you may still be reading situations well — and it is not adding up to anything, because there is no steady ground under it and no place to set what you learn down.

What restores a center is not more effort. It is contact. Someone with one honest thing they are carrying, and you sitting beside them without handling it from a step away. Not the tuning of it — the staying. Notice you are still there while it goes on, with your own shape intact. The scattering eases when one real thing gets through and you let it stay unfinished.

cells.tense: You are blending and adapting all day long and calling it just how you are.
cells.act: join the practice the others keep
cells.ask: Show up to a class, a group, a regular thing you have been circling from the outside. Go twice before you decide whether it fits.
cells.core:
You read what a gathering needs and adjust without noticing you are doing it, so the skill stays unnamed — not stated to others, and not to yourself. Anyone watching can see it happen. They watch you find the temperature and move to it, and they could probably describe it better than you could. From where you sit it is just what a person does.

Before you had a method, you belonged to something. There was a practice with other people in it, and you learned by keeping it, not by analyzing it. Go back to one of those — a class, a group, a standing thing that others show up for. Show up twice. You will see the same tuning you do all day, except this time there is something to belong to and other people doing it with you, and it stops being invisible.
cells.sheetLine: You have been tuning what a gathering needs and calling it nothing.
